title: Real-time Logistics Fleet Tracking
business: A regional logistics company managing a fleet of delivery vehicles that require constant location updates for dispatchers.
problem: Dispatchers rely on manual page refreshes to see vehicle positions, leading to stale data and inefficient routing decisions during peak traffic hours.
solution: Server-Sent Events (SSE) enables a persistent, unidirectional HTTP connection from the server to the dispatcher dashboard, pushing location updates immediately as they arrive from GPS sensors without requiring client-side polling.
steps: Configure the server to set the Content-Type header to text/event-stream.
Maintain an open HTTP connection between the client EventSource object and the server.
Format outgoing data messages with the data: prefix followed by the JSON payload.
Implement client-side event listeners to handle incoming location updates and update the UI dynamically.
outcome: Dispatchers gain a fluid, real-time view of fleet operations, allowing for proactive adjustments to delivery routes and improved response times to traffic incidents.
limitation: SSE is strictly unidirectional, meaning the client cannot send data back to the server over the same connection; developers must check the browser console for connection closure events to trigger manual reconnection logic.

questions.question: In Real-time Logistics Fleet Tracking, why is SSE preferred over traditional polling?

It eliminates the need for manual page refreshes to see vehicle positions.
It provides a bidirectional communication channel for GPS data.
It automatically reduces the number of GPS sensors required.

The client cannot send data back to the server over the same connection.
The browser cannot handle text/event-stream content types.
